title: Welcome Andy Baker | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z announces former US Deputy National Security Advisor Andy Baker as an Advisor to its Global Affairs mission. Neuberger argues foreign governments want to build with American tech and that AI, defense, cyber, energy and infrastructure companies need geopolitical guidance.

insights.claim: Technology is now central to how countries defend themselves, grow their economies, and provide for their citizens, so American innovators carry both an opportunity and a responsibility to build technologies that strengthen America and its allies.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Frames tech sales abroad as strategic alignment, supporting demand for US tech in allied markets.
insights.quote: Technology is now central to how countries defend themselves, grow their economies, and provide for their citizens

insights.claim: Government leaders worldwide tell a16z they want to adopt American innovation and build with US firms through shared capabilities, joint ventures, and partnerships tailored to their countries' needs.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Signals foreign sovereign demand for co-development structures rather than pure exports.

insights.claim: Turning foreign government interest into real collaboration requires understanding what governments are trying to accomplish, how they make decisions, and where technology makes a practical difference.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Go-to-market abroad is gated by government decision-making literacy, not just product quality.

insights.claim: a16z has added Andy Baker, former US Deputy National Security Advisor, as an Advisor to its Global Affairs mission, advising both Global Affairs and portfolio companies.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Shows a16z deepening its Washington-connected national security bench.

insights.claim: Baker served as Deputy National Security Advisor to President Trump and National Security Advisor to Vice President Vance, previously advised then-Senator Vance, and spent over a decade as a Foreign Service Officer including Afghanistan and NATO headquarters in Brussels.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Close ties to the current administration's foreign policy circle may give portfolio companies access.

insights.claim: a16z established Global Affairs to connect founders' ambitions with the needs of America and its allies, with practical work: helping countries access and build with critical technologies and helping companies navigate unfamiliar markets.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Indicates a16z treats geopolitical brokering as a portfolio-support function and competitive differentiator.

themes.theme: Sectors where government and commercial priorities converge

insights.claim: Companies in AI, defense, cybersecurity, energy, and critical infrastructure increasingly operate in markets where government priorities and commercial opportunities are closely connected.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Names the sectors where geopolitical exposure and state demand shape returns.
insights.locator: That experience matters for our founders

insights.claim: Founders in these sectors need to understand how their technology addresses a country's strategic needs, which partnerships can help them succeed, and how geopolitical developments may affect their plans.
insights.speaker: Anne Neuberger
insights.so_what: Geopolitical risk is a core diligence factor for these companies' international plans.
insights.locator: That experience matters for our founders
